newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended a nervous trading session at its best intraday levels after the market took a breather following a rollercoaster ride on Thursday.

Forex traders said late dollar inflows helped the currency firmer in the afternoon but the market was still bruised after confusing signals on the rand from the South African Reserve Bank on Tuesday which saw many players hurt.
They said the market was struggling to find direction and all eyes were focused on Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's adjustment budget speech at 1239 GMT on Thursday for fresh impteus.
"The market is very nervous and there's no clear direction...it's very difficult to call levels," a forex trader at one of the four leading banks said.

Another senior trader noted that the market had stabilised after losing around seven cents on Tuesday on comments by Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals that there might have been a slight "over-adjustment" in the rand this year.
However, it managed to retrace virtually all of its losses on late bullish comments by Stals.

Stals said in a statement on Wednesday that quotes attributed to him were "absolutely correct as far as I can recall", but that there had been an "unfortunate but forgiveable misunderstanding" over his remarks about the rand.
The forex trader said the currency market appeared to be happy that Stals did not mean "anything untoward" about the rand and had found a new 4.38 to 4.45 range to trade in.
"One thing's for sure, the rand won't go screaming through the 4.38 level on the downside but it looks as if it has found new levels between 4.38 and 4.45 to trade in," the trader said.
Against the crosses, the rand had last recovered to 7.1915/2040 against sterling from 7.2832/2912 late on Tuesday. It was trading at 0.3810/3816 marks from 0.3758/3726 marks previously.
Long bonds ended a jittery day near their previous closing levels after the market weakened by a massive 30 basis points on Tuesday.
At 1450 GMT the benchmark R150 bond was at 15.07 percent from 15.06 percent late on Tuesday.
A senior bond trader said the market had taken a "well-earned rest" after its recent bull run.
"There's quite a lot of nervousness ahead of Manuel's budget adjustment chat on Thursday although on the whole the expectations are for a positive undertone," the trader noted
He said the market would still be in a retracement phase on Thursday if it moved above the 15.12 percent level.
"But if it ranges between 14.95 to 15.12 percent I would say we're seeing consolidation."
Traders said December PPI data -- due out at 0900 GMT on Thursday -- was likely to be overshadowed by Manuel's budget adjustment speech.
A Reuters consensus forecast of 11 economists predicted the producer price index (PPI) would grow 0.9 percent month-on-month or 8.7 percent year-on-year from 8.5 percent in November.

Foreigners sold a net 243.48 million rands worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 241.81 million on Monday, the Bond Exchange said, while nominal cumulative turnover was 8.69 billion rand on Tuesday from 8.67 billion rand on Monday.
South Africa's money market fell back to 9.588 billion rand on Tuesday from 10.275 billion rand on Monday, the Reserve Bank said.
Three-month NCDs rates were quoted slightly easier at between 16.40 to 16.65 percent from between 16.45 to 16.65 percent while the 90-day BA rate was unchanged at between 15.80 to 16.05 percent bid.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
